guard_order: In handle the forward sits after the internal-caller test (a non-internal caller is refused with FIRM_BINDING before any forward), after the bucket_for failure that both the literal map and the function environment must satisfy, and after the service or internal allowed-firm narrowing (verified = selected), immediately before the firm-claim match.
failure: Any exception, any FunctionError or a missing payload from the forward answers NOT_READY through refuse, with no class, message or body.
logging: _forward logs and prints nothing and never edits the event; the existing caller-class line of the allowed-firm narrowing is written before the forward, as before.
words: The 49F read function now forwards a Cottonwood request, and only a Cottonwood request, to the Cottonwood read function. served.py gains one literal one-entry map, an injectable forward_invoke port on Entry, the method Entry._forward, and one change in handle: when the firm cannot be mapped to a bucket, the request is forwarded only if the literal map names that firm and this function's environment names the target; otherwise FIRM_BINDING as before. The forward runs after the internal-caller test and the allowed-firm narrowing, so the caller is admitted as for any firm. The original event goes to the target untouched and its reply comes back untouched. NOT PROVEN: nothing was deployed; the Cottonwood function does not exist yet; the real proxy event across a real Lambda invoke was not exercised; and whether a staff read of a Cottonwood account is served without a Cottonwood ownership map is unknown until the pair's probe.
